TOURISM & PLACE · METHODOLOGY

Understand the story behind the data.

How the data was collected, what the measures mean and where comparisons need care.

DATA COLLECTION

How this dataset was assembled

We used published national aggregates, not personal records or a survey conducted by this website. The original energy CSV determined the 16-country sample. Tourism observations were added by matching country names and country codes, with each measure’s unit, year, definition and source retained.

  1. Retrieve: Download OECD inbound-tourism tables, Eurostat monthly nights and bed-place data, and World Bank/ICAO airline totals through their public data interfaces. Transcribe 2024 arrivals and travel receipts from OECD’s published tables and the China and India statistical releases.
  2. Supplement: Record Canada’s published national resident-survey result and one illustrative UNESCO-listed place per country. Preserve all 49 original energy fields.
  3. Check: Confirm 16 country records, units, reporting years and missing-value handling; verify the original energy values are unchanged. Calculate seasonal shares only when all 12 months are present. Do not fill gaps with estimates.
  4. Publish: Save a static CSV with 96 fields, including source URLs and notes. Sources were accessed on 20 September 2026. This is not a live feed; tourism mostly refers to 2024 and airline activity to 2023. Review newer releases before operational decisions.

Country briefs provide source links beside individual measures. View archived public data downloads ↗ · Read the source and processing notes ↗

Missing data, bias and uncertainty

Selection and reporting bias

The sample was chosen for energy consumption, not tourism representativeness. It overrepresents large economies and cannot support worldwide conclusions. Monthly data cover only three European countries; the resident result covers Canada only. Small accommodation providers may fall below reporting thresholds, and a single heritage example does not represent a country’s full visitor offer.

Uncertainty and geographic limits

Survey estimates, provisional values, revisions, exchange rates and different arrival definitions limit comparability. The UK-labelled series has a 2024 Great Britain coverage break. Confidence intervals are not supplied in this dashboard; small differences should not be treated as statistically meaningful. National averages hide local and seasonal differences. Missing data mean unverified in this release, not zero activity or zero impact.

Privacy: This dashboard uses public aggregate statistics. It has no accounts, personal-data submission forms, analytics trackers or location requests. Country searches, comparisons and usage calculations stay in your browser and are not saved by the application. Do not enter names, contact details, medical information, precise personal locations or other sensitive data. The hosting provider and external source websites have their own access-log and privacy practices.
Read the methodology and limits of comparison

Coverage is the original 15 energy-consuming countries plus Croatia, not a worldwide tourism ranking. Tourism measures use a 2024 baseline; airline activity uses 2023 and electricity rates use December 2025. Newer releases may exist. All source links and metric years remain in the CSV.

Arrivals count trips, not unique people. Overnight tourists, visitors including same-day trips, and accommodation arrivals are separate measures. The UK-labelled OECD series has a 2024 coverage break involving Great Britain. Comparisons of size are descriptive, not destination performance scores.

Travel receipts are current-USD balance-of-payments travel exports, excluding international passenger transport. They are not profit, total tourism economic contribution, domestic spending, or government revenue. Exchange rates affect comparisons. We do not divide receipts by arrivals because the populations and methods differ.

Seasonality uses monthly domestic and international accommodation nights from Eurostat. Bed places measure reported accommodation capacity; national size thresholds can exclude small providers. Inbound accommodation nights from OECD mix visitor surveys and accommodation surveys. These are not occupancy rates and cannot be combined into an occupancy estimate.

Air passengers are carried by nationally registered airlines on domestic and international routes. They are not inbound tourists, airport traffic, route availability, or a measure of local public transport. Attraction examples are illustrative heritage places, not popularity rankings or operating-status recommendations.

Resident survey coverage is limited to a verified Canadian national result. Missing values mean unavailable in this release, never zero. We do not infer resident views, local capacity or environmental impacts from visitor volumes or energy mix. Regional monthly counts, local transport use, housing data and representative resident surveys are still needed for local management.

Original energy data and tools are retained. Business electricity prices assume 1,000,000 kWh/year and are not hotel-specific tariffs. Domestic electricity generation mix is not consumed-electricity mix; “Other” includes nuclear. Sources are credited in each country brief and in the downloadable records.
